subject: BlueHarbor Dedicated reserved-commit: term structure & ramp plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Grey <marcus.grey@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueHarbor Dedicated reserved-commit: term structure & ramp plan

Marcus —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a formalized offer based on the usage profile you shared (daily token volume, peak concurrency, and acceptable latency SLOs). High level options included in the PDF and pricing spreadsheet:

- Term options: 12 / 24 / 36 months (price per GPU-hour steps down at longer terms)
- Ramp windows: 4 / 8 / 12 week start gates for initial capacity activation
- Throughput guarantees: committed baseline qps and burst policy for 30% above baseline
- Credits: onboarding credit and one-time migration credit if start delayed >30 days

Callouts specific to BlueHarbor: based on your forecast we modeled a 24-month reserved commit with a 2-stage ramp (50% in first 6 weeks, 100% by week 12) as the most cost-efficient path. That configuration yields the 18% effective discount vs on-demand Dedicated rates and preserves burst capacity for peak windows.

Please review the attached BH_Committed_Offer_v1.pdf and the pricing table. If procurement has constraints on term or start date, tell me the constraint (exact target % discount or max term) and I’ll work with finance on a counter that keeps your unit economics favorable.

Next steps: once you confirm the target term/ramp we’ll generate an SOW + DocuSign that includes the activation calendar and milestone-based invoicing.

—
Irene Choi

Subject: Re: BlueHarbor Dedicated reserved-commit: term structure & ramp plan

Irene —

Appreciate the clear options and the modeling. Procurement reviewed and has two asks before we can greenlight: 

1) Pricing: BH procurement needs a deeper discount to justify a 24-month commit. Target is ~22% off list (your 18% is close but we need to get to that 22% threshold for internal ROI sign-off).
2) Start flexibility: our internal compliance change may push our effective start by 6–8 weeks. We cannot accept full billing until capacity is active; we can accept milestone billing but need a guaranteed start window and a protected hold on reserved capacity for a maximum 12 weeks from signature.

If Greenwood (sorry — Redwood) can meet 22% on a 24-month and include a hold-to-start clause (no billing until activation but reserved capacity held for up to 12 weeks with a one-time 30% reduced onboarding credit), we can move to Exec review this week.

—Marcus

Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: FW: BlueHarbor Dedicated reserved-commit: term structure & ramp plan

Team —

Looping you in. BlueHarbor is pushing for a 22% effective discount on a 24-month commit and wants the ability to delay activation up to 12 weeks post-signature without being invoiced (they will accept milestone billing after activation). Proposal items from them:

- Target: 22% off list for 24-month reserved commit
- Activation hold: reserved capacity held for up to 12 weeks post-signature; billing starts on activation; if start delayed past 12 weeks we either (a) release capacity or (b) reduce onboarding credit and charge a nominal holding fee.
- They will accept SOW with milestone invoicing tied to activation.

My ask: can finance/ops accommodate a 22% list discount for a 24-month? If not, can we offer a structured concession (e.g., 18% baseline + a usage-tier rebate that nets them ~22% at forecasted utilization)? Also need guidance on the hold-to-start language and whether we can commit to holding capacity without billing for 12 weeks.

Also: they indicated start might be in late-August given compliance work — that pushes our typical 4–8 week ramp windows out.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick sync if easier.

—Irene

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: BlueHarbor Dedicated reserved-commit: term structure & ramp plan

Irene —

Thanks for the read. Quick thoughts: finance is willing to be flexible here because BlueHarbor is a strategic account and the forecasted committed consumption is high. We can offer the following counter that preserves revenue while meeting their procurement ask: 

Counteroffer (recommended):
- Term: 24 months
- Effective discount: 20% off list up front + a utilization-based rebate that can add up to 2.5% back to them quarterly if they hit the forecast utilization bands (nets ~22.5% at target usage).
- Activation hold: we will hold reserved capacity for up to 10 weeks post-signature at no charge. If activation occurs after week 10 and before week 14, we apply a one-time holding fee equal to 5% of first month committed invoice. After week 14 we reserve the right to reallocate capacity (but we will offer a 30-day notice and discuss alternatives).
- Ramp: two-stage ramp (50% allocation upon activation, remaining 50% by week 12). Billing begins at activation.
- SLA & throughput: commit baseline throughput as modeled; provide 30% burst above baseline and a defined P99 latency target in the SOW.

Rationale: the comp mix keeps our committed revenue intact while giving BH procurement the headline number they need to close. The utilization rebate is standard and drives alignment. The hold-to-start is softened to 10 weeks (we can stretch to 12 with a modest holding fee). 

Irene: please propose this as a revised offer and see if procurement will accept 20%+rebate structure or whether they need a hard 22% up front. If they push for an immediate 22% up front, we need a short internal approval but can consider it if they commit to a faster activation schedule.

—Aditya
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Revised offer: 24-month reserved commit + ramp & activation hold (BlueHarbor)

Marcus / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clear guidance. Per our internal review we can extend the following revised offer for the 24-month reserved commit: 

Summary of revised terms:
- Term: 24 months
- Pricing: 20% off list at signature + a utilization-tier rebate program (quarterly true-up) that can add up to 2.5% if forecasted utilization tiers are met (effective potential discount up to ~22.5% at target usage).
- Activation hold: reserved capacity held for up to 10 weeks post-signature with no charge. If activation occurs in weeks 11–14, a one-time holding fee equal to 5% of the first invoice will apply. Past week 14 we will discuss reallocation options with 30 days' notice. Billing starts on activation.
- Ramp: 50% capacity at activation, remaining 50% ramped to full allocation by week 12 after activation.
- Throughput/SLA: baseline throughput guaranteed; 30% burst above baseline; P99 latency target documented in SOW.
- Onboarding credit: standard onboarding credit reduced by 30% if activation is delayed beyond week 10.

Attachments: updated offer (BH_Committed_Offer_v1.pdf — revised), pricing table (Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Table.xlsx).

Next steps: If you confirm verbally, I’ll ask legal to produce an SOW and we’ll generate DocuSign (link below) with milestone-based invoicing tied to activation. Please flag any final procurement/finance questions — we can also set a short call with Aditya and Marissa to expedite.
